questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking (bilingual with french is also okay hehe), and nice liveable and lively city!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Can highly recommend Montréal and McGill as a destination!!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Decently easy. We got emails reminding us of every thing we needed to know beforehand. I had a friend from KU coming to the same destination and it helped a lot having a person to chat to about deadlines, things that needed to be sorted. So good idea to connect a bit with someone beforehand (if you can of course).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Only the emails that got sent to us from the international student office at McGill, but that was very helpful!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Good opportunities for help and meeting other international students. Many events and such!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Quite hard. I heard from the earlier reports from KU students that there was plenty of housing at great prices but it was very hard once i got there. People from there were telling me there was kind of a housing crisis (kinda like most big cities have so nothing out of the ordinary) but it was definetely doable. There are a bunch of good facebook groups for finding housing in areas close to uni. If you search "McGill off campus housing" or something like that there are a good ammount of groups to find housing for students :) BEWARE OF SCAMMERS!!! There are a lot and they can seem very convincing. DO A VIDEO CALL WITH THEM TO BE SURE!! 

i recommend posting on the groups with information about yourself and some pictures and what you are looking for. Then you will get messages from people. Much more efficient than scrolling through every post on all groups in my opinion.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
That there can be a LOT of variety in the housing you get. I spoke to many people that found rooms in amazing big townhouses for around 950 CAD while i payed 1000 CAD for a room in a tiny little apartment. So it varies a lot. 

In regards to searching early to secure a place, it is very hard. If you are searching on groups, people typically only post ads for the coming month or so. So i was posting myself on all the groups and got almost 0 response until a month or so before leaving. So if you can find one early, then great. But it is a lot harder to find when it is months away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can heavily recommend the "plateau" area for living! Very lively and filled with bars and events for young people. Very Nørrebro like i would say. A bunch of nice parks and relatively close to uni. Also Mile end was nice! Downtown is very much just big buildings with corporations without much soul so i dont recommend living there unless you like that. The places outside of downtown are way nicer and more lively. Downtown has no real culture.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is like "first come first serve" for the courses mostly. There is a time and then you want to apply as fast as you can. I think the exchange students get an early pass to the registration which is nice. But make sure you have courses lined up that you want to apply for BEFORE the deadline and that you know that they fit together in the weekly schedule. Cause if you apply a bit later, some of the courses will be full.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is like "first come first serve" for the courses mostly. There is a time and then you want to apply as fast as you can. I think the exchange students get an early pass to the registration which is nice.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I didnt really need help so i'm not sure. But im sure you can write or call to someone to help you with it all.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the ones i wanted :)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As i said before, make sure you have courses that fit in the schedule ready before the registration. There is like a website with schedule planning called Visual Schedule Builder (VSB) where you can put in the classes and you can see them in the weekly schedule and see if they fit. Very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very proffessional and high quality.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level very similar to UCPH (For biology) I was a third year student and mostly took third year classes and the level was good. Not too hard and not too easy. But i think it varies a lot in depending on the field.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. But for many of the courses i took it was only lectures for in person classes. No session for assignments or something. but it was fine.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Pretty much all of them. They were very well organised and i learned a lot! 

BIOL 300 was a very dry course. -NAME REDACTED- doesnt speak english too well and it was only lectures, Midterm and FInal. No assignments or quizzes to get grade points like there was in the others.

questions.answer: Housing was a little more expensive than i thought but other than that it was normal.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were clubs and sports for almost anything at McGill so tons of opportunity to meet new people with the same interests.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were clubs and sports for almost anything at McGill so tons of opportunity to meet new people with the same interests.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking and going on trips outside of the city. Especially in the fall! Tons of pretty nature to go explore a little outside of Montreal. Mont Tremblant was a very beautigul hike to the top! highly recommend. Or renting a shed somewhere in a forest with friends is also highly recommended. And other than that just go out and explore all the differents parts of the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See my answer above.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. People are sooo nice there! But try to meet with some locals also to really understand ;) Go on some dates or however you want to meet new people :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didnt attend any clubs myself but i think they are a great way to meet people!! And also try to make some friends in class if you can. It can be hard when it is mostly lectures, but try your best ;) People are very nice and typically want to hang out outside if school also. Going on dates from dating apps (hinge for me) was also super nice. Very good way to learn about people living there and meeting amazing people you can hangout with (if all goes well of course hehe) throguhout your stay. I met the sweetest girl who i hung out with  througout my stay.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really. Very few people dont speak english so that wasnt a problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everyone is so friendly. And also the fact that each part of the city is so different and has their own style and vibe. Fun to explore them all.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make an effort to find people you can explore the city with and have fun with. It can be very hard to find people, but talking to people on facebook groups from UCPH and meeting them in Montreal is a great way to start!! 

Go outside of the city also for the pretty nature!

And just enjoy and experience as much as you can while you are there! You will regret not doing enough during your stay :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Can't think of something.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a core friend group (we were 4 people from Denmark) and experiencing the city and all it has to offer together!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably just studying for finals after some hard midterms. And for my courses there were always weekly assignments and quizzes that counted towards the grade which made it so that i was a little bit on edge and stressed about school after the first two months.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
